title: Narratives to Numbers: Large Language Models and Economic Policy Uncertainty
abstract: arXiv:2511.17866v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study the implications of adopting machine-generated data in economic analysis. Rather than taking the data-generating process as given and correcting estimates econometrically, we evaluate how upstream modeling and researcher choices shape downstream estimates. Revisiting the Economic Policy Uncertainty index, we find that large language models fine-tuned on human audit labels identify nearly twice as many auditor-flagged articles as keyword-based alternatives and are robust to noisy text and linguistic drift. Varying classifier, threshold, and aggregation choices produces substantial differences not only in performance but in what the index captures, reshaping the relationship between policy uncertainty and returns.

translated_title: 从叙事到数字：大语言模型与经济政策不确定性
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在经济分析中采用机器生成数据的影响。我们不是将数据生成过程视为既定并通过计量经济学方法纠正估计值，而是评估上游建模和研究者选择如何塑造下游估计结果。通过重新审视经济政策不确定性指数，我们发现基于人工审计标签微调的大语言模型识别出的审计人员标记文章数量几乎是基于关键词方法的近两倍，并且对噪声文本和语言漂移具有鲁棒性。改变分类器、阈值和聚合方式的选择不仅在性能上产生显著差异，还会改变指数所捕捉的内容，从而重塑政策不确定性与收益率之间的关系。
tldr: 基于人工审计标签微调的大语言模型在构建经济政策不确定性指数时，识别审计标记文章的数量几乎是关键词方法的两倍，且不同的建模选择会显著改变指数的内涵及其与市场收益的关系。
en_tdlr: Fine-tuned large language models identify nearly twice as many auditor-flagged articles as keyword-based methods in constructing the Economic Policy Uncertainty index, and varying upstream modeling choices substantially reshapes what the index captures and its relationship with stock returns.
